quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver should:

options.text: Not stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where they can see 200 feet in each direction, even if they enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled area.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the main traveled area. Both vehicles need adequate space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: When another driver is trying to pass your car, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: Seat belts help drivers by:

options.text: Helping them control their vehicles on curved roads.
Reducing injury and death risk in a crash.
Helping them control their vehicles on rough roads.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt properly reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts also help you stay in control on curved or rough roads and when avoiding a collision.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating vehicles.
Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles coming from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again in case you missed any vehicles.

questions.question: Driving faster:

options.text: Increases your field of vision.
Decreases your field of vision.
Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
Does not affect your field of vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decreases your field of vision.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision decreases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: When is it illegal to pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: You must use the shoulder of the road to pass a vehicle that is driving below the speed limit.
You are on a one-way, two-lane road and the vehicle ahead has stalled.
You are on a multilane highway and the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit.
You are on a two-way, two-lane road and the vehicle ahead is turning left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the shoulder of the road to pass a vehicle that is driving below the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Never leave the roadway to pass another vehicle. Only pass on the right when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always look through your back window when backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are near. Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up or out of a driveway.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beams.
High beams.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Sharp toward the curb.
Slightly to the right.
Sharp away from the curb.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharp away from the curb when parking uphill. This keeps your vehicle from rolling into traffic. If there is no curb, turn the wheels sharp toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: High speeds.
Slow speeds.
Driving at night.
Driving uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds.
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force if you crash.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic signals or signs, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, check all directions, then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from your right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Sound your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait for traffic to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unusual conditions ahead.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. Text on the sign confirms it is a no passing area.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but has no emergency signals on. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without using its siren or lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians go first, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn you about railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is ahead. Watch for trains.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks if someone offers you one while you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving crashes is to decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol changes your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices once you have been drinking.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving is harder and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer levels often. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: You have a green light and want to turn left, but traffic is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn left because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for the other traffic to pass first. You can enter the intersection to get ready to turn if the light is green and no car ahead of you is turning left.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane one-way street or highway, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start from the left lane when turning left on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your car may not turn easily due to its forward motion. Slow down before entering a curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop at a yield sign if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to the same speed as the freeway traffic. This helps you merge smoothly and safely. Vehicles entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on it.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your car.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils shrink. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see well enough to drive safely.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to the lane you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to your current lane. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: When may you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your hazard lights.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when you have an emergency.

questions.question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and get ready to stop. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until it passes before crossing.

questions.question: Your gas pedal gets stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the gas pedal sticks, the engine will keep running even if you lift your foot off the pedal. Turn off the ignition carefully to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then use the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines are doubled in this work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that the area ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the right side of the road with lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and move quickly to a lane farther away.
Slow down and move safely away from the lane next to the emergency vehicle.
Keep your speed and stay in the right lane.
Pull over to the right and stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and move safely away from the lane next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the right with flashing lights, slow down right away. If the road has two or more lanes in your direction, move to a lane that is not next to the emergency vehicle, if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you cannot stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you cannot stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and try to stop before you enter the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely, drive through carefully.
